A group is a collection of player characters who have banded together to complete a common goal. Forming a group enables players to chat privately among themselves, share XP, collectively complete quest objectives and achievements, manage the distribution of loot from mobs, among other things. In World of Warcraft there are two types of groups: ;Party :A group consisting of at least 2 and up to 5 players. Party is the default type of group and is used primarily for completing 5-man dungeons and group quests, or to band together for any simple purpose. ;Raid :A group consisting of at least 2 and up to 40 players. Raids must be created out of a party and are used primarily for completing raid

Group loot is a loot distribution system similar to round robin that allows players to roll for higher quality items. The party or raid leader chooses what the threshold is for items (green , blue , or purple ). This system is best for a Pickup Group (PuG).

.]] Grunts are the basic warriors of the Horde and the orcish clans. They are typically equipped with mighty axes and battle-worn armor. A group of guilds is just that: several guilds that have grouped together for some common purpose. Usually formed to fill out 40-man raid groups, so PUGs of such a large size are avoided. The politics of a group of guilds can be complicated and require a united leadership to be effective. Not a commonly used term but one that encompasses such terms as "guild alliances", "guild groups", or "multi-guild groups".

Group buffs are a mana- and time-efficient means to distribute buff spells. Usually group buffs have a longer duration than the spell that they distribute. They almost always require a reagent. Distribution occurs as a group buff is cast on a target; characters that are "similar" to the target will also get the buff. Similarity depends on whether the spell is a party buff or a greater blessing.
